The '''1931 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 46th staging of the All-Ireland [[hurling]] championship since its establishment by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] in 1887. The championship began on 1 May 1932 and ended on 4 September 1932.

[[Cork GAA|Cork]] were the [[1931 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]], however, they were defeated in the provincial series of games. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the title following a 3–3 to 2–3 victory over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[1932 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Roll of Honour |publisher=The GAA website |access-date=21 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110905085701/http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |archive-date=5 September 2011 }}</ref>

==Teams==

A total of twelve teams contested the championship, the same number of participants from the [[1931 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|previous championship]]. There were no new entrants.

==Championship statistics==

===Scoring===

*Widest winning margin: '''19 points''' 
**Clare 8–3 – 2–2 Kerry (<small>''Munster semi-final, 3 July 1932''</small>)
*Most goals in a match: '''10''' 
**Clare 9–4 – 4–14 Galway (<small>''All-Ireland semi-final, 14 August 1932''</small>)
*Most points in a match: '''23''' 
**Clare 9–4 – 4–14 Galway (<small>''All-Ireland semi-final, 14 August 1932''</small>)
*Most goals by one team in a match: '''9''' 
**Clare 9–4 – 4–14 Galway (<small>''All-Ireland semi-final, 14 August 1932''</small>)
*Most goals scored by a losing team: '''5''' 
**Offaly 5–2 – 6–8 Laois (<small>''Leinster quarter-final, 8 May 1932''</small>)
*Most points scored by a losing team: '''6''' 
**Galway 4–14 – 9–4 Clare (<small>''All-Ireland semi-final, 14 August 1932''</small>)

===Miscellaneous===

* The Munster quarter-final clash of Cork and Waterford and the Munster semi-final clash of Clare and Kerry, both scheduled for 5 June 1932, are postponed.
* Clare win the Munster title for the first time since [[1914 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1914]].
* Clare overcame a halftime deficit of 13 points in the All Ireland semifinal against Galway (2-00 4-07) by scoring 7–04 in the second half to Galway's 0-07. It remains (July 2022) the largest halftime deficit clawed back in an All Ireland semifinal.
* There are a number of first-ever meetings. The All-Ireland semi-final between Clare and Galway is their first ever championship clash, while Clare and Kilkenny meet for the first time in the subsequent All-Ireland final.
